title: Velocity-driven Disney motion smear and squash-stretch
blurb: One ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas draws a live draggable studio card with area-preserving squash-stretch, 16-tap directional velocity smear and a leading/trailing chromatic RGB trail, snapping back to 1:1 crispness and synced hit-testing at rest.
question: Can one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas apply area-preserving squash-stretch, 16-tap directional smear and chromatic RGB trails to a draggable HTML card from instantaneous velocity while keeping buttons and text inputs clickable at rest and in motion?
result: Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 (2026-11-27): all 6 live checks pass at 412 px (DPR 2.625, 0.91 MP canvas, 7.27 MB initial, 16.78 MB peak, 0 errors) and 960 px desktop (DPR 2). Under diagonal (+1.2, -0.9) motion, stretch reaches 1.45x and squash 0.69x (product 1.00) with trailing smear luminance rising from 13 to 124 (perpendicular 13) and separated trailing blue vs leading red fringes, while updateElementGeometry() keeps +1 Ping, colour pills and text input editing accurate across displaced settles. Chrome 159 on Android and npm run check:jank stay not verified.
